content.content:
# harbor-dispatch

Berth planning, cargo manifests and arrival estimates for the terminal operations team.

The code is TypeScript and runs directly on Node 26; there is no build step and there are no
runtime dependencies. Port and vessel reference data live under `registry/`. Incidents are
tracked in the ops queue.
---OPS---
incidents.pack
---SRC---
src/generated/registry.ts
src/berths/schedule.ts
src/berths/fit.ts
src/eta/transit.ts
src/eta/local.ts
src/cargo/manifest.ts
src/cargo/hazmat.ts
src/ports/locode.ts
src/ports/registry.ts
src/types.ts

content.text:
All tests pass, including the new ones matching INC-219's acceptance criteria exactly.

Now let's clean up the temp file and check final diff.

INC-219 is fixed: **`localArrival`** in `src/eta/local.ts` was hardcoding `"UTC"` instead of using the destination port's timezone from the registry, so all arrival times were shown in UTC regardless of the port (e.g., Singapore arrivals shown 8 hours early). I changed it to use `port.timezone`, added regression tests for the exact cases from the incident report (Singapore and Rotterdam), and confirmed the full test suite (`npm run check`) passes.
